identificationSites.name: Anthracite / Smith Hill / Cloud City Coal Camp & Mine Complex
overview: Historic anthracite mine and Cloud City landscape; mine, rail load-out and camp are linked components.

identificationSites.name: Baldwin / Mount Carbon Coal-Mining Town & Mine Complex
overview: Historic Baldwin coal-mining settlement and railroad landscape; old and later Baldwin phases remain distinct.

identificationSites.name: Colorado-Yule Marble Quarry, Mill & Electric Railroad Complex
overview: Parent identification for the Yule Marble quarry, Marble mill and electric railroad components.

identificationSites.name: Crested Butte Historic District / Mining & Coal Town
overview: Historic coal-mining town and district; individual mines and rail features remain linked components.

identificationSites.name: Crystal Mining Townsite / Crystal City
overview: Historic Crystal townsite with surviving building fabric; Crystal Mill remains a linked distinct component.

identificationSites.name: Doctor Mine & Spring Creek / Bogan’s Camp Complex
overview: Doctor Mine and its linked worker-camp landscape form the parent Scan target.

identificationSites.name: Ohio City / Eagle City Mining Town
overview: Historic Ohio City mining town; Eagle City is preserved as the predecessor settlement.

identificationSites.name: Pieplant / Pie Plant Mill & Mining Camp
overview: Historic mine-mill-camp complex in the Pieplant area.

identificationSites.name: Schofield Mining Camp / Townsite
overview: Historic Schofield mining camp and townsite; exact remnant count remains a research detail.

identificationSites.name: Standard Mine / Standard Metals Mine
identificationSites.location: Ruby Mining District / Crested Butte area
overview: Historic Standard/Standard Metals mine complex with extensive workings and surface remnants.

identificationSites.name: Star Mine Complex
overview: Historic Star Mine complex with surviving shaft house, bunkhouse, sawmill and mining equipment.

identificationSites.name: Taylor Park B-24E Bomber Crash Site
overview: Sensitive WWII aviation crash and funerary site; identification only, with no disturbance or approach guidance.

identificationSites.name: Aberdeen Quarry & Quarry Camp / D&RG Spur Complex
identificationSites.location: Aberdeen Quarry area southwest of Gunnison, Gunnison County, Colorado
overview: Aberdeen is a documented late-nineteenth-century granite quarry, worker camp, and Denver & Rio Grande spur complex. Quarry remains, the former townsite, and surviving camp material support the property as a basic Scan identity.

identificationSites.name: Floresta / Ruby Coal Mine & Mining Camp Complex
identificationSites.location: Floresta / Ruby area, Gunnison County, Colorado
overview: Floresta and Ruby form a documented coal-mine and company-camp landscape associated with Colorado Fuel & Iron operations. Mine, camp, and railroad remnants support the parent complex as a basic Scan identity.

identificationSites.name: Gothic Mining Townsite
overview: Gothic is a documented 1879 silver-mining townsite with surviving historic buildings and a stable modern identity through the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory. The townsite remains distinct from individual mines and buildings within the broader landscape.

identificationSites.name: Irwin / Ruby Camp Mining Town
identificationSites.location: Irwin / Ruby Camp area, Gunnison County, Colorado
overview: Irwin, historically known as Ruby Camp, is a documented mining-town landscape in the Ruby District. The parent identity includes the camp and its relationship to nearby workings such as the Forest Queen while keeping individual mine components distinct.

identificationSites.name: Ohio Creek Extension Railroad Grade & Rock Culvert Complex
identificationSites.location: Ohio Creek area, Gunnison County, Colorado
overview: The Ohio Creek Extension is a documented unfinished railroad-engineering landscape with an intact grade and three surviving stone culverts. These linked features support identification as one basic Scan complex.

identificationSites.name: Pitkin / Quartzville Mining Town
overview: Pitkin, originally known as Quartzville, is a documented historic mining town with strong railroad and surrounding-mine relationships. The town serves as the parent identity while related transportation and mining features remain distinct components.

identificationSites.name: Tin Cup / Tincup / Virginia City Mining Town
overview: Historic Tin Cup mining town, also known as Tincup and historically Virginia City; established around the nineteenth-century precious-metals district.

identificationSites.name: Crystal Mill / Sheep Mountain Power House
overview: The 1892 Sheep Mountain powerhouse, commonly called Crystal Mill, used water power to support compressed-air mining equipment for nearby Crystal-area mines.

identificationSites.name: Alpine Tunnel West Portal & Alpine Tunnel Station Complex
overview: Gunnison-side west portal and station complex of the historic Alpine Tunnel railroad district, including surviving railroad-engineering remnants.

identificationSites.name: Bon Ton Hotel / Pitkin Mining-Era Hotel
overview: Surviving Pitkin hotel rebuilt in 1904 after a 1903 fire, associated with the mining town and Alpine Tunnel-era rail traffic.

identificationSites.name: Fairview Peak Fire Lookout
identificationSites.category: Forest Service / Fire Lookout / Historic Infrastructure
overview: Historic 1912 Forest Service fire lookout on Fairview Peak, later stabilized and restored as an important high-elevation lookout structure.

identificationSites.name: Crested Butte D&RG Railroad Depot
overview: Surviving Denver & Rio Grande depot dating to the early 1880s, serving freight and passengers in the Crested Butte mining and coal district.

identificationSites.name: Dorchester Guard Station / Dorchester Townsite Remnant
identificationSites.category: Historic Forest Service / Ghost Town Remnant
overview: 1905 log structure surviving from the former Dorchester townsite; historically served community and later Forest Service functions.

identificationSites.name: Spencer School / Spencer Ghost Town Schoolhouse
identificationSites.category: Mining Town / Rural School / Ghost Town Remnant
overview: 1902 one-room school complex surviving from the Spencer mining community and ghost-town landscape.

identificationSites.name: Gunnison River Bridge I
overview: Historic 1920s rigid-connected Pratt through-truss bridge associated with early Colorado state-highway development.

identificationSites.name: Gunnison River Bridge II
overview: Historic 1920s rigid-connected Pratt through-truss bridge, paired with Gunnison River Bridge I as a surviving early highway-engineering resource.

identificationSites.name: Fairview Schoolhouse / Ohio Creek School District No. 10
overview: Surviving 1906 Fairview Schoolhouse associated with Ohio Creek School District No. 10 and the surrounding historic rural and mining-area community.
